en: And Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: Al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil—and he is Ibn 'Ubaydullah—narrated to us, from al-Zuhri: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik informed me, from his uncle, 'Ubaydullah ibn Ka'b—and he was Ka'b's guide when he lost his sight, and he was the most knowledgeable of his people and the most retentive among them regarding the narrations of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—he said: I heard my father, Ka'b ibn Malik—and he was one of the three whose repentance was accepted—narrating that he never stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in any expedition that he undertook except two expeditions. And he pursued the hadith, and he said in it: 'And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) set out for the expedition with many people, exceeding ten thousand, and no preserving register compiled them.'

And 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to me: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Muslim, the nephew of al-Zuhri, narrated to us, from his uncle, Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik informed me that 'Ubaydullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik—and he was Ka'b's guide when he went blind—said: I heard Ka'b ibn Malik narrating his account when he stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in the Battle of Tabuk. And he pursued the hadith, and he added in it over Yunus: 'Rarely would the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) intend an expedition except that he disguised it with another, until it was that expedition.' And in the narration of the nephew of al-Zuhri, he did not mention Abu Khaythamah and his catching up with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).
